What is a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR), and in which cells is it expressed?
정답: ['Synthetic transmembrane protein (receptor)', 'Expressed at the surface of immune effector cells reprogrammed in vitro or in vivo']
atom: A chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) is a synthetic transmembrane protein expressed at the surface of immune effector cells that have been reprogrammed either in vitro or in vivo.

True or False?
"The DNA sequence encoding a CAR fuses domains derived from immunoglobulins with a chain of the T cell receptor and, usually, domains from costimulatory molecules that participate in T cell activation."
정답: True
atom: A CAR is encoded by a DNA sequence that combines domains from immunoglobulins, one chain of the T cell receptor, and typically domains from costimulatory molecules involved in T cell activation.

A patient with B-ALL relapses after CD19-directed therapy. Sequencing of the relapsed blasts reveals a point mutation in the CD19 gene, and the resulting CD19 protein is not properly anchored to the cell membrane, so little CD19 is detectable on the blast surface.
Is this an instance of surface antigen loss caused by a CD19 point mutation? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: In B-ALL, point mutations in CD19 can cause nonfunctional anchoring of the CD19 protein to the cell membrane and consequently loss of surface antigen.

A company manufactures CAR-T cells in large batches from a single healthy donor's T cells and edits out TRAC. The product is cryopreserved and stored. A patient with rapidly progressing lymphoma is infused from this stock within days. The patient's own T cells are never collected, and no individualized production run is needed, so there are no weeks of waiting and no risk that the patient's cells fail to expand.
Is this an allogeneic off-the-shelf CAR-T approach that avoids the limitations of autologous T cell manufacturing (personalized production, weeks of manufacturing time, risk of manufacturing failure)? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: Allogeneic off-the-shelf CAR-T cells avoid certain limitations of autologous T cells, namely a personalized production process, several weeks of manufacturing time, and the risk of manufacturing failure.

During the CAR-T cell treatment workflow, at what point is bridging therapy given relative to leukapheresis and lymphodepletion?
정답: ['After leukapheresis', 'Before lymphodepletion (during CAR-T cell manufacturing)']
atom: Bridging therapy is therapy given after leukapheresis and before lymphodepletion during CAR-T cell manufacturing.

True or False?
"Bridging therapy is mainly intended to keep the underlying disease from progressing uncontrollably while the CAR-T cells are being manufactured, before they are infused."
정답: True
atom: The primary goal of bridging therapy is to prevent uncontrolled progression of the underlying disease during the manufacturing period before CAR-T cell infusion.

True or False?
"It has been clearly established that an even more intensive lymphodepleting regimen is required in solid tumours."
정답: False
atom: Whether an even more intensive lymphodepleting regimen is needed in solid tumours is currently unknown.

A cohort of patients received anti-CD19 and anti-CD22 CAR-T cells, which attack B-lineage precursors. During long-term follow-up, hypogammaglobulinaemia or agammaglobulinaemia is described as a rare event, seen only in isolated patients after CAR-T treatment.
Is this description consistent with the typical long-term finding of hypogammaglobulinaemia/agammaglobulinaemia after anti-CD19/anti-CD22 CAR-T therapy? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: Because anti-CD19 and anti-CD22 CAR-T cells attack B-lineage precursors, long-term hypogammaglobulinaemia or agammaglobulinaemia is commonly seen in patients after CAR-T cell treatment.

A laboratory stains peripheral blood from a patient 14 days after CAR-T infusion with an anti-CAR antibody together with antibodies against CD4, CD8, CD45RA, CCR7, PD1, TIM3 and Lag3 in a single flow cytometry panel. They analyse the CAR-positive gate for CD4/CD8 ratio, naïve versus memory phenotype, and exhaustion marker expression.
Does this approach allow the CAR-T cells to be characterized by T cell subtype, differentiation, and exhaustion status? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: Combining CAR staining with other surface markers in flow cytometry allows CAR-T cells to be characterized by T cell subtype (CD4/CD8), differentiation (naïve versus memory), and exhaustion (PD1, TIM3, Lag3).

A developer implements a spin lock on a single atomic flag. Lock acquisition uses an atomic exchange with memory_order::relaxed, and lock release uses an atomic store of 0 with memory_order::relaxed. Ordinary non-atomic data updated inside the critical section is expected to be protected from data races by the lock.
Is this a correct lock implementation that protects the guarded memory updates from data races? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: A relaxed memory ordering cannot be used to implement a lock correctly, because lock-guarded memory updates rely on acquire-release ordering for protection from data races.

While an atomic_ref referencing a particular object exists in SYCL, what must be true of all accesses to that object?
정답: ['All accesses must be atomic', 'performed via an instance of atomic_ref']
atom: While any atomic_ref referencing a specific object exists, all accesses to that object must occur atomically via an instance of atomic_ref.

True or False?
"Even when a kernel only writes to a buffer, the buffer's original content may still be transferred to the device, since the runtime cannot be sure that the kernel will overwrite every value in the buffer."
정답: True
atom: Even if a kernel only writes to a buffer, the buffer's original content may still be moved to the device, because there is no guarantee that the kernel will write all values in the buffer.

How can a SYCL array reduction over an array of size $N$ be understood in terms of scalar reductions, and why?
정답: ['Equivalent to $N$ scalar reductions with the same data type and operator', 'Each component of the array reduction is independent']
atom: Each component of an SYCL array reduction is independent, so an array reduction on an array of size $N$ is equivalent to $N$ scalar reductions with the same data type and operator.

When can a SYCL kernel rely on the result of a reduction having been written back to the original variable?
정답: ['Not guaranteed until the kernel has completed', 'Cannot assume the value is written back during kernel execution']
atom: The result of a SYCL reduction is not guaranteed to be written back to the original variable until the kernel has completed.

True or False?
"In SYCL, work-groups have local memory for exchanging data among their work-items, but sub-groups have no equivalent dedicated memory space of their own."
정답: True
atom: Unlike work-groups, sub-groups have no dedicated memory space (no sub-group local memory) for exchanging data among their work-items.

How can work-items in a SYCL sub-group exchange data directly without explicit memory operations?
A) Using shuffle operations, which are available only between work-items of different work-groups
B) Using a dedicated sub-group local memory space declared in the kernel
C) Using a subset of the group algorithms known as shuffle operations, but only through explicit global memory stores and loads
D) Using a subset of the group algorithms colloquially known as shuffle operations
정답: D
atom: Work-items in a sub-group can exchange data directly, without explicit memory operations, using a subset of the group algorithms colloquially known as shuffle operations.

In SYCL, what defines an error as an "asynchronous error", i.e., who detects it and how does its occurrence relate to the host program's command execution?
정답: ['Detected by the SYCL runtime (or an underlying backend)', 'Occurs independently of the execution of commands in the host program']
atom: In SYCL, asynchronous errors are errors detected by the SYCL runtime (or an underlying backend) that occur independently of the execution of commands in the host program.

In SYCL, what is a kernel bundle?
정답: ['A container', 'Holds the SYCL kernels or functions used by an application']
atom: A SYCL kernel bundle is a container for the SYCL kernels or SYCL functions used by an application.

A SYCL application has a kernel bundle that has been fully compiled to device code for a specific GPU. The bundle is ready to be launched on that GPU without any further compilation step.
Is this kernel bundle in the executable state? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: A kernel bundle in the executable state is fully compiled to device code and is ready to be executed on the device.

True or False?
"Explicitly requesting an executable-state kernel bundle is expensive even if all kernels were ahead-of-time compiled or already just-in-time compiled, because the bundle must still be recompiled."
정답: False
atom: Explicitly requesting an executable-state kernel bundle is effectively free if all kernels were ahead-of-time compiled or were already just-in-time compiled, because all kernels would already be in the executable state.

What does it mean for a kernel $k: X \rightsquigarrow Y$ between measurable spaces to be s-finite?
정답: ['k is a countable sum (sequence-indexed) of kernels', 'each kernel in the sum is a finite kernel']
atom: A kernel $k:X\rightsquigarrow Y$ between measurable spaces is s-finite if there is a sequence $k_1,k_2,\ldots$ of finite kernels with $\sum_{i=1}^\infty k_i = k$.

True or False?
"A kernel $k: X \rightsquigarrow Y$ is finite if for each $x$ there is a finite $r_x \in [0,\infty)$, which may depend on $x$, such that $k(x,Y) < r_x$."
정답: False
atom: A kernel $k:X\rightsquigarrow Y$ is finite if there is a finite $r\in[0,\infty)$ such that $k(x,Y)<r$ for all $x$.

Let $X=\mathbb{R}$ with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, let $Y=\{a,b\}$ with the power-set $\sigma$-algebra, and let $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be a non-Borel set. Define $k(x,U)=1$ if $x\in V$ and $a\in U$, and $k(x,U)=0$ otherwise. For every fixed $x$, $k(x,-)$ is a measure on $Y$ (either the Dirac measure at $a$ or the zero measure). However, $k(-,\{a\})$ is the indicator function of $V$.
Is $k$ a kernel from $X$ to $Y$? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: A kernel from $X$ to $Y$ is a function $k : X \times \Sigma_Y \to [0,\infty]$ such that each $k(x,-)$ is a measure and each $k(-,U)$ is measurable in $x$.

A probabilistic program $P$ is run with nondeterministic choices resolved by a scheduler. For every scheduler $\sigma$, the expected termination time $\mathbb{E}^{\sigma}_{\mathbf{x}_{init}}[Term]$ from the initial state is a finite number (although the bound may differ between schedulers).
Is $P$ finitely terminating, i.e. positively almost-surely terminating? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: A probabilistic program is finitely terminating (also called positively almost-surely terminating) if the expected termination time $\mathbb{E}^{\sigma}_{\mathbf{x}_{init}}[Term]$ is finite under every scheduler $\sigma$.

What conditions must a discrete-time stochastic process $\{X_n\}$ adapted to a filtration $\{\mathcal{F}_n\}$ satisfy to be a ranking supermartingale (RSM)?
정답: ['Integrability and a.s. lower bound: $\\mathbb{E}[|X_n|]<\\infty$ and $X_n\\ge K$ for some $K\\le 0$', 'Ranking condition: $\\mathbb{E}[X_{n+1}\\mid\\mathcal{F}_n]\\le X_n-\\epsilon$ whenever $X_n\\ge 0$ (for some $\\epsilon>0$)']
atom: A ranking supermartingale (RSM) is a discrete-time stochastic process $\{X_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ adapted to a filtration $\{\mathcal{F}_n\}$ for which there exist reals $\epsilon>0$ and $K\le 0$ such that, for all $n$, $\mathbb{E}[|X_n|]<\infty$, almost surely $X_n\ge K$, and almost surely $\mathbb{E}[X_{n+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_n]\le X_n-\epsilon\cdot\mathbf{1}_{X_n\ge 0}$.

In every possible execution from this initial configuration, $x$ at $\ell_1$ only ever takes values in $\{0,1,\dots,5\}$. In probability theory, what is a coupling of two sub-distributions $\mu_1$ over $\mathcal{A}_1$ and $\mu_2$ over $\mathcal{A}_2$?
정답: ['A sub-distribution $\\mu$ over the product $\\mathcal{A}_1\\times\\mathcal{A}_2$', 'Its first marginal equals $\\mu_1$ and its second marginal equals $\\mu_2$']
atom: A probabilistic coupling of two sub-distributions $\mu_1$ over $\mathcal{A}_1$ and $\mu_2$ over $\mathcal{A}_2$ is a sub-distribution $\mu$ over pairs $\mathcal{A}_1\times\mathcal{A}_2$ whose first and second marginals equal $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$, i.e. $\pi_1(\mu)=\mu_1$ and $\pi_2(\mu)=\mu_2$.

True or False?
"A sub-distribution $\mu$ over $\mathcal{A}_1\times\mathcal{A}_2$ is a witness for the $\mathcal{R}$-lifting of $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$ if $\mu$ is a coupling of $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$ and its support is a superset of $\mathcal{R}$, i.e. $\mathcal{R}\subseteq\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$."
정답: False
atom: A sub-distribution $\mu$ over $\mathcal{A}_1\times\mathcal{A}_2$ is a witness for the $\mathcal{R}$-lifting of $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$, for a relation $\mathcal{R}\subseteq\mathcal{A}_1\times\mathcal{A}_2$, if $\mu$ is a coupling of $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$ and $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)\subseteq\mathcal{R}$.

For two sub-distributions $\mu_1,\mu_2$ over the same set $\mathcal{A}$, what is the relationship between $\mu_1=\mu_2$ and the lifting of the equality relation $\mu_1\,(=)^\sharp\,\mu_2$?
A) $\mu_1=\mu_2$ only implies $\mu_1\,(=)^\sharp\,\mu_2$, but the converse fails in general
B) $\mu_1=\mu_2$ if and only if $\mu_1\,(\neq)^\sharp\,\mu_2$
C) $\mu_1\,(=)^\sharp\,\mu_2$ holds if and only if $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ are independent
D) $\mu_1=\mu_2$ if and only if $\mu_1\,(=)^\sharp\,\mu_2$
정답: D
atom: Two sub-distributions $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ over the same set are equal if and only if they are related by the lifting of the equality relation, $\mu_1\,(=)^\sharp\,\mu_2$.

In quantitative information flow, what is a hyper-distribution produced by a channel acting on a prior, and what are its outcomes and the probabilities attached to them?
정답: ['A distribution on posterior distributions (distribution over distributions)', 'Each posterior is the prior conditioned on a particular output (normalised joint-matrix column)', 'Weights are the output marginal probabilities']
atom: A hyper-distribution is a distribution on posterior distributions: the output marginal of a channel's joint input-output distribution, taken as a distribution over the posterior input distributions obtained by conditioning the prior on each particular output (the normalised joint-matrix columns).

Program P leaks the Boolean secret $b$ by outputting $b$, and program Q leaks it by outputting $\mathrm{not}\ b$. Neither changes the state, and an adversary who knows the source code can deduce $b$ exactly in both cases. A theorist models both using hyper-distributions that abstract away the actual observed output values.
Under this hyper-distribution semantics, are P and Q given the same denotation (and hence regarded as behaviourally equal)? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: Hyper-distributions abstract away the actual values of observations, retaining only the deductions an adversary can make, so that programs such as observing $b$ and observing $(\mathrm{not}\ b)$ are treated as the same, and two programs are behaviourally equal just when their denotations are equal (full abstraction).

In quantitative equational logic, what is a quantitative $\Omega$-algebra, and what condition must the interpretation of each operation symbol satisfy?
정답: ['Carrier is an extended metric space $(A,d)$', 'Each operation symbol $f:\\kappa$ is interpreted as a function $A^\\kappa\\to A$ (from the $\\kappa$-fold product of the metric space)', 'Each interpretation must be non-expansive']
atom: A quantitative $\Omega$-algebra consists of an extended metric space $(A,d)$ together with a non-expansive interpretation $f_\mathcal{A}: A^\kappa\to A$ of each operation symbol $f:\kappa\in\Omega$, where $A^\kappa$ is the $\kappa$-fold cartesian product of the metric space $A$.

정답: ['Probability that e evaluates to the same value n', 'in the unreliable evaluation as in the fully reliable evaluation']
atom: In Rely, the reliability of an integer expression e is the probability that it evaluates to the same value n in an unreliable evaluation as in the fully reliable evaluation.

atom: Rely's analysis conservatively approximates the reliability of a computation by considering only the scenario in which the unreliable evaluation encounters no faults, and ignores the scenario in which faults occur but the correct value is still returned by chance.

Is the terminal dendroidal set $N\mathbf{Com}$, the nerve of the commutative operad, a normal dendroidal set?
정답: ['No, it is not normal']
atom: The terminal dendroidal set $N\mathbf{Com}$ is not normal.

What kind of object is the Boardman–Vogt resolution of an operad $P$, in terms of its colours and its relation to $P$?
정답: ['An operad W(P) with the same set of colours as P', 'Comes with an operad map $\\varepsilon: W(P)\\to P$ that is the identity on colours']
atom: For an operad $P$, the Boardman–Vogt resolution is an operad $W(P)$ with the same set of colours as $P$, together with a map of operads $\varepsilon: W(P)\to P$ that is the identity on colours.

True or False?
"An operation of $W(P)(c_1,\dots,c_n;c)$ is represented by a tree with colour-labelled edges and vertices labelled by operations of $P$, where every edge has a length in $[0,1]$ and the external edges (leaves and root) all have length 0."
정답: False
atom: An operation of $W(P)(c_1,\dots,c_n;c)$ is represented by a tree with leaves labelled $c_1,\dots,c_n$, root labelled $c$, edges labelled by colours, vertices labelled by operations of $P$, and in addition every edge given a length in $[0,1]$ such that the external edges (leaves and root) all have length 1.

Operations of the Boardman–Vogt resolution $W(P)$ are represented by trees with coloured, length-labelled edges and vertices labelled by operations of $P$. Which three kinds of identification generate the equivalence relation on these trees?
정답: ['Isomorphisms of trees respecting the labellings (colours, operations, lengths)', 'Contraction of edges of length zero', 'Erasure of vertices labelled by a unit operation']
atom: The equivalence relation on length-labelled trees defining $W(P)$ is generated by three kinds of identification: isomorphisms of trees respecting labellings (including lengths), contraction of edges of length zero, and erasure of vertices labelled by a unit operation.

True or False?
"Let $A$ be a shuffle of trees $S$ and $T$, and let $(s,t)$ label an edge of $A$ that is not a leaf. Then the vertex above this edge has inputs labelled either $(s_1,t),\dots,(s_n,t)$, where $s_1,\dots,s_n$ are the inputs of the vertex above $s$ in $S$, or $(s,t_1),\dots,(s,t_m)$, where $t_1,\dots,t_m$ are the inputs of the vertex above $t$ in $T$."
정답: True
atom: In a shuffle $A$ of trees $S$ and $T$, each non-leaf edge labelled $(s,t)$ has a vertex above it whose inputs are labelled either $(s_1,t),\dots,(s_n,t)$, with $s_1,\dots,s_n$ the inputs of the vertex above $s$ in $S$, or $(s,t_1),\dots,(s,t_m)$, with $t_1,\dots,t_m$ the inputs of the vertex above $t$ in $T$.

True or False?
"For the tensor product of dendroidal sets, there are internal hom objects $\mathbf{Hom}(Y,Z)$ such that maps $X\otimes Y\to Z$ correspond naturally to maps $X\to\mathbf{Hom}(Y,Z)$."
정답: True
atom: The tensor product of dendroidal sets has inner hom objects $\mathbf{Hom}(Y,Z)$ adjoint to it, characterized by natural isomorphisms $\mathbf{dSets}(X\otimes Y,Z)\simeq\mathbf{dSets}(X,\mathbf{Hom}(Y,Z))$.

Let $X=\Lambda^1[2]$, the simplicial set consisting of two composable non-degenerate edges $a:0\to1$ and $b:1\to2$ and no 2-simplex filling them. Define $\tau_1(X)$ as follows: the objects are the vertices of $X$, and arrows $x\to y$ are classes of 1-simplices $f$ with $d_1f=x$ and $d_0f=y$, where $f\sim f'$ if some 2-simplex $e$ has $d_2e=f$, $d_1e=f'$ and $d_0e=s_0y$. Consider the evident comparison functor $\tau_1(X)\to\tau(X)$ to the homotopy category.
Is this functor an isomorphism of categories for this $X$, as it is for inner Kan complexes? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: If $X$ is an inner Kan complex, the homotopy category $\tau(X)$ is isomorphic to the category $\tau_1(X)$ whose objects are the vertices of $X$ and whose arrows $x\to y$ are equivalence classes of 1-simplices $f$ with $d_1f=x$ and $d_0f=y$, where $f\sim f'$ if some 2-simplex $e$ has $d_2e=f$, $d_1e=f'$ and $d_0e=s_0y$.

정답: False
atom: If $\mathbf{P}$ is a simplicial operad such that $\mathbf{P}(x_1,\dots,x_n;y)$ is a Kan complex for every tuple of colours $(x_1,\dots,x_n,y)$, then its homotopy-coherent nerve $w^*\mathbf{P}$ is an ∞-operad.

What data and axioms define a Reedy category, in particular what kind of factorization must every morphism admit?
정답: ['Category R with a degree function d: ob(R) → N and two subcategories R^+ (positive) and R^- (negative) of morphisms', 'Every morphism factors as f = p∘n with p positive and n negative', 'This factorization is unique up to isomorphism']
atom: A Reedy category is a category R equipped with a degree function $d:\mathrm{ob}(R)\to\mathbb{N}$ and subcategories $R^+$ (positive) and $R^-$ (negative) of morphisms, such that every morphism factors as $f=p\circ n$ with $p$ positive and $n$ negative, uniquely up to isomorphism.

True or False?
"Let R be a Reedy category and Y → X a map of E-valued presheaves on R. If for every object r of R the map from Y(r) to the pullback of Y(∂r) → X(∂r) ← X(r) is a fibration (resp. trivial fibration) in E, where X(∂r) is the limit of X over all strictly positive morphisms into r, then Y → X is a Reedy fibration (resp. Reedy trivial fibration)."
정답: True
atom: For a Reedy category R and a map Y→X of E-valued presheaves, the map Y is a Reedy (trivial) fibration if, for each object r of R, the matching map $Y(r)\to Y(\partial r)\times_{X(\partial r)}X(r)$ is a (trivial) fibration in E, where $X(\partial r)$ is the limit of X over strictly positive morphisms into r.

Let R be a Reedy category and E a model category. Y → X is a Reedy fibration in E^{R^{op}}, and Y(r) → X(r) is a weak equivalence in E for every object r of R except one object r_0, where Y(r_0) → X(r_0) is not a weak equivalence.
Is Y → X a Reedy trivial fibration? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: A Reedy fibration $Y\to X$ is a Reedy trivial fibration if and only if $Y(r)\to X(r)$ is a weak equivalence in $\mathcal{E}$ for every object $r$ of $R$.

A researcher wants to measure the equilibrium pressure of the circulation when there is no flow. In an animal model, she stops the heart and measures the pressure that equilibrates throughout the whole circulatory system, including the systemic vessels, the heart chambers and the pulmonary circulation, all in open communication.
Does this measurement correspond to mean systemic pressure (Pms) as it is defined, i.e., equilibrium pressure in the systemic circulation alone, with the heart and pulmonary circulation excluded? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: Mean systemic pressure (Pms) is defined as the equilibrium pressure in the systemic circulation in the absence of any flow, ignoring the heart and pulmonary circulation (e.g., by clamping the aorta and venae cavae).

True or False?
"A fluid bolus increases venous return and cardiac output provided that stressed volume and mean systemic pressure rise substantially, with a marked concurrent rise in right atrial pressure, and the ventricles operate on the steep portion of the cardiac function curve."
정답: False
atom: A fluid bolus raises venous return and cardiac output only if stressed volume and mean systemic pressure increase significantly with minimal change in right atrial pressure and both ventricles operate on the steep portion of the cardiac function curve.

How does positive pressure ventilation affect right atrial pressure, the pressure gradient for venous return, and venous return itself, and through what mechanism?
정답: ['Pleural pressure rises and is partially transmitted to the right atrium, raising right atrial pressure', 'The venous return pressure gradient falls, so venous return decreases']
atom: During positive pressure ventilation, pleural pressure increases and is partially transmitted to the right atrium, so right atrial pressure rises, the pressure gradient for venous return falls, and venous return decreases.

During mechanical ventilation, how does tidal breathing-related rise in pleural pressure affect right ventricular afterload and output?
A) It reduces transmural pulmonary vascular pressure, raising right ventricular afterload and increasing right ventricular output.
B) It reduces transmural pulmonary vascular pressure, lowering right ventricular afterload and decreasing right ventricular output.
C) It reduces transmural pulmonary vascular pressure, raising right ventricular afterload and decreasing right ventricular output.
D) It increases transmural pulmonary vascular pressure, raising right ventricular afterload and decreasing right ventricular output.
정답: C
atom: During mechanical ventilation, tidal breathing increases pleural pressure, which reduces transmural pulmonary vascular pressure and thereby raises right ventricular afterload and decreases right ventricular output.

A patient is placed on positive pressure ventilation with PEEP, so intrathoracic and pleural pressures rise. The transmural pressure of the left ventricle falls, and to a lesser degree that of the intrathoracic aorta falls, while transmural pressure in the abdominal aorta stays higher. This facilitates flow from the intrathoracic to the abdominal compartment.
Does this patient show a net reduction in left ventricular afterload? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: During positive pressure ventilation or PEEP, rising intrathoracic pressure lowers the transmural pressure of the left ventricle and, to a lesser extent, of the intrathoracic aorta, while transmural pressure in the abdominal aorta remains higher, producing a net reduction in left ventricular afterload.

In the Stewart physicochemical approach to acid-base balance, plasma [HCO3-] and pH are treated as dependent variables. Which three independent variables determine them?
정답: ['Total CO2 content', 'Strong ion difference (SID)', 'Total concentration of weak nonvolatile acids (Atot)']
atom: In the Stewart physicochemical approach to acid-base balance, plasma [HCO3-] and pH are dependent variables determined by three independent variables: total CO2 content, strong ion difference (SID), and the concentration of weak nonvolatile acids (Atot).

A clinician analyzing a patient's plasma uses the routinely measured values Na+ 140, K+ 4, Ca2+ 2.5 and Mg2+ 1 mEq/L as the strong cations, and Cl- (the main strong anion) 105 mEq/L as the strong anion. She computes the difference between the summed strong cations and the summed strong anions.
Is the value she calculates the apparent strong ion difference (SID) in the Stewart approach? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: In the Stewart approach, the apparent strong ion difference (SID) is the sum of the routinely measured strong plasma cations (Na+, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+) minus the sum of the routinely measured strong plasma anions (mostly Cl-).

In the Stewart approach, what is the effect on plasma SID and on acid-base status of infusing large volumes of zero-SID fluids such as 0.9% saline, dextrose, or mannitol solutions, and by what mechanism does it occur?
정답: ['Plasma SID is reduced', 'Via admixture and equilibration with the plasma', 'Pushes acid-base balance toward metabolic acidosis']
atom: In the Stewart approach, infusing large volumes of zero-SID fluids (saline with equal [Na+] and [Cl-], or dextrose or mannitol solutions without strong ions) reduces plasma SID by admixture and equilibration, pushing acid-base balance toward metabolic acidosis.

In critical care fluid management, what are the four dynamic phases of fluid therapy described by the ROSE concept?
정답: ['Resuscitation', 'Optimization', 'Stabilization and evacuation']
atom: The ROSE concept describes four dynamic fluid phases of fluid therapy: resuscitation, optimization, stabilization and evacuation.

In critical care fluid management, what is Late Goal-Directed Fluid Removal (LGFR), also called de-resuscitation, and what methods and time window define it?
정답: ['Active fluid removal using diuretics or renal replacement therapy with net ultrafiltration', 'Started within the first week of ICU stay']
atom: Late Goal-Directed Fluid Removal (LGFR), also called de-resuscitation, is defined as active fluid removal with diuretics or renal replacement therapy with net ultrafiltration, started within the first week of ICU stay.

A fluid-overloaded ICU patient with ARDS is hemodynamically stable. The team plans active fluid removal by running slow low efficiency hemodialysis (SLED) with a set net ultrafiltration target each session.
Is this an acceptable way of achieving active fluid removal in de-resuscitation? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: Active fluid removal in de-resuscitation can be achieved either by judicious use of diuretics or by ultrafiltration using continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) or slow low efficiency hemodialysis (SLED).

How is intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) defined in terms of intra-abdominal pressure (IAP)?
정답: ['Sustained increase in IAP', 'Equal to or greater than 12 mmHg']
atom: According to the Abdominal Compartment Society (WSACS), intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) is defined as a sustained increase in intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) equal to or greater than 12 mmHg.

True or False?
"Abdominal compartment syndrome is defined as a sustained increase in intra-abdominal pressure above 12 mmHg that is associated with new organ dysfunction or failure."
정답: False
atom: Abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) is defined as a sustained increase in IAP above 20 mmHg that is associated with new organ dysfunction or failure.

The model is built on serial measurements of blood hemoglobin dilution.
Is this model an example of volume kinetics? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: Volume kinetics is an adaptation of pharmacokinetic theory that makes it possible to analyze and simulate the distribution and elimination of infusion fluids.

In the skin of a mouse fed a high-salt diet, interstitial tonicity is elevated. Macrophages release VEGF-C, which binds VEGF Receptor 3 on lymphatic endothelial cells. Over the following weeks the lymphatic capillary network grows more extensive and interstitial fluid clearance capacity increases.
Is this process an example of VEGF-C-driven lymphangiogenesis? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: VEGF-C acting on VEGF Receptor 3 stimulates lymphangiogenesis, extending the lymphatic capillary network and enhancing the capacity for interstitial fluid clearance.

What is the purpose of the RDF Mapping Language (RML), and what kinds of input does it cover?
정답: ['Expresses customized mapping rules to generate RDF', 'Input can be heterogeneous data structures, formats and serializations']
atom: The RDF Mapping Language (RML) expresses customized mapping rules from heterogeneous data structures, formats and serializations to RDF.

"RML is a subset of R2RML that narrows R2RML's scope by adding support for heterogeneous data."
정답: False
atom: RML is a superset of R2RML that aims to extend R2RML's applicability and broaden its scope by adding support for heterogeneous data.

What does data integration aim to provide, and what characteristics of the underlying data sources make this challenging?
정답: ['uniform access to multiple data sources', 'sources are distributed (decentralised), autonomous, and heterogeneous']
atom: Data integration is the process of providing uniform access to a set of distributed (decentralised), autonomous, and heterogeneous data sources.

A company builds a tool that connects to three separate databases (a CRM, a billing system, and an HR system). The tool lets analysts open each database in its own native schema through a single login page, but it defines no shared schema: customer records from the CRM, billing, and HR systems remain in their own structures and naming conventions, and analysts must reconcile them manually.
Is this tool a data integration system in the sense of providing a global (mediated) schema that gives a reconciled view of the data in the different sources? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: A data integration system provides a global (mediated) schema that gives a reconciled view of all data available in the different data sources.

A data integration system has a global schema G with relations Movie(title, year) and Director(name, title). Its mapping defines each global relation as a query over the sources: Movie(t, y) is computed from source relation imdb_films(t, y, d), and Director(n, t) from imdb_films(t, y, n). No source element is itself described by a query over G.
Is this mapping specified using the Local-as-View (LAV) approach? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: Under the Local-as-View (LAV) approach, data sources are described as views over the global schema, with the mapping rules in $M$ associating a query over the global schema $G$ to each element of the source schema $S$.

What does a federated query processing system provide, and over what kind of data sources?
정답: ['A unified access interface', 'Over autonomous, distributed, and heterogeneous data sources']
atom: A federated query processing system provides a unified access interface to a set of autonomous, distributed, and heterogeneous data sources.

True or False?
"A federated query engine takes a query written against the global schema and rewrites it into an equivalent query expressed in the schemas of the individual data sources."
정답: True
atom: The role of a federated query engine is to transform a query expressed in terms of the global schema (the federated query) into an equivalent query expressed in the schemas of the data sources (the local query).

A federation contains three autonomous SPARQL endpoints: one for drugs, one for diseases, and one for clinical trials. A user poses a single query over the federation. The engine splits it into three subqueries, one sent to each endpoint, and the overall query is the union of these subqueries over the individual sources.
Is this an instance of the main objective of federated query processing, i.e., transforming a query on a federation into a query composed of subqueries over individual data sources? (Yes/No)
정답: Yes
atom: The main objective of federated query processing is to transform a query posed on a federation of data sources into a query composed of the union of subqueries over individual data sources of the federation.

What are the four conceptual sub-problems (components) of federated query processing?
정답: ['Data source description', 'Query decomposition and source selection', 'Query planning and optimization, and query execution']
atom: Federated query processing conceptually involves four main sub-problems: data source description, query decomposition and source selection, query planning and optimization, and query execution.

Let $A$ be the minimal operator $-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}$ with domain $H^2_0(0,1)$ in $L^2(0,1)$, so $A^*$ is the maximal operator with domain $H^2(0,1)$. Pick a function $g\in L^2(0,1)$ with $g\notin H^2(0,1)$, for example $g(x)=|x-\tfrac12|^{1/2}$. Define $\widetilde A$ on $\mathrm{dom}(\widetilde A)=H^2_0(0,1)\dotplus\mathrm{span}\{g\}$ by $\widetilde A h=Ah$ for $h\in H^2_0(0,1)$ and $\widetilde A g=0$.
Is $\widetilde A$ a proper extension of $A$, that is, does $\widetilde A$ belong to $\mathrm{Ext}(A)$? (Yes/No)
정답: No
atom: A proper extension of a symmetric operator $A$ is an operator $\widetilde A$ with $\mathrm{dom}(A)\subset\mathrm{dom}(\widetilde A)\subset\mathrm{dom}(A^*)$, and the set of all proper extensions is denoted $\mathrm{Ext}(A)$.

Given a boundary triplet $\{\mathcal{H},\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1\}$ for $A^*$, how can all proper extensions of the symmetric operator $A$ be parametrized? Describe the parametrizing objects and the map.
정답: ['Parametrized by linear relations $\\Theta$ in $\\mathcal{H}$ via $\\Theta\\mapsto A_\\Theta=A^*\\restriction\\{f\\in\\mathrm{dom}(A^*):(\\Gamma_0 f,\\Gamma_1 f)\\in\\Theta\\}$', 'This map is a bijection between $\\mathrm{Ext}(A)$ and the set of all linear relations in $\\mathcal{H}$']
atom: Given a boundary triplet for $A^*$, the map $\Theta\mapsto A_\Theta=A^*\restriction\{f\in\mathrm{dom}(A^*):(\Gamma_0 f,\Gamma_1 f)\in\Theta\}$ is a bijective correspondence between the proper extensions of $A$ and the set of all linear relations in $\mathcal{H}$.

Let $\{\mathcal{H},\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1\}$ be a boundary triplet for $A^*$, and let $A_\Theta$, $A_{\widetilde\Theta}$ be self-adjoint extensions of $A$. For $p\in(0,\infty]$, when does $(A_\Theta-i)^{-1}-(A_{\widetilde\Theta}-i)^{-1}$ lie in the Schatten class $\mathfrak{S}_p$?
A) Only if $(\Theta-i)^{-1}-(\widetilde\Theta-i)^{-1}\in\mathfrak{S}_p(\mathcal{H})$, with no converse implication in general.
B) If and only if $(\Theta-i)^{-1}-(\widetilde\Theta-i)^{-1}\in\mathfrak{S}_p(\mathcal{H})$.
C) If and only if $\Theta^{-1}-\widetilde\Theta^{-1}\in\mathfrak{S}_p(\mathcal{H})$.
D) If and only if $(\Theta-i)^{-1}-(\widetilde\Theta-i)^{-1}\in\mathfrak{S}_{2p}(\mathcal{H})$.
정답: B
atom: If $A_\Theta=A_\Theta^*$ and $A_{\widetilde\Theta}=A_{\widetilde\Theta}^*$, then for every $p\in(0,\infty]$ the resolvent difference $(A_\Theta-i)^{-1}-(A_{\widetilde\Theta}-i)^{-1}$ lies in the Schatten class $\mathfrak{S}_p$ if and only if $(\Theta-i)^{-1}-(\widetilde\Theta-i)^{-1}\in\mathfrak{S}_p(\mathcal{H})$.

"A Dirichlet form $\mathfrak{t}$ is recurrent if and only if the constant function $\mathbb{1}$ belongs to the extended Dirichlet space $\mathrm{dom}(\mathfrak{t}_e)$ and $\mathfrak{t}_e[\mathbb{1}]=1$."

atom: A Dirichlet form $\mathfrak{t}$ is recurrent if and only if the constant function $\mathbb{1}$ belongs to the extended Dirichlet space $\mathrm{dom}(\mathfrak{t}_e)$ and $\mathfrak{t}_e[\mathbb{1}]=0$.

"Being quasi-isometric is an equivalence relation on the class of metric spaces."
정답: True
atom: Quasi-isometries define an equivalence relation between metric spaces.
